$note: Key facts about the two scripted Blender camera-body models (blender/build_dslr.py, blender/build_mirrorless.py) for the app and tests to check the .glb exports against, without re-deriving them from the Blender scene. Frame: millimeters, sensor plane at z = 0, lens axis along -z, y up, x to the camera's right as seen from behind (docs/PANE.md). See blender/common.py's module docstring for the Blender-Z-up -> glTF-Y-up axis mapping used at export time.
$textures: Surface finish ships beside the GLBs in models/textures/, not inside them (an embedded texture makes three's GLTFLoader throw under node, which the GLB tests hit). Each finished material carries glTF extras {normalMap: a path relative to models/, normalScale, uvTileMm}, and its meshes carry box-projected UVs (TEXCOORD_0), one texture tile per uvTileMm millimeters. The app loads the PNG as that material's normalMap (RepeatWrapping, flipY false, NoColorSpace) with normalScale from the extras.

dslr.depthNote: The model's 78.5 mm runs from the rear plate to the grip front. The eyepiece housing and eyecup stand 7.8 mm behind the plate: the model's own length, since no published eyepiece length was found, set at the most that CIPA's 10% rule (as reported) lets a maker leave out of a 78.5 mm depth. Nikon does not say whether its figure includes them. So the two bodies' depths are not directly comparable: the DSLR's 78.5 mm leaves its eyepiece out, the mirrorless body's 83 mm includes its eyecup.
dslr.shapeNote: Traced from Nikon's manual drawings: the outline width, the prism's cheeks, the control positions. The model's own, generic shapes: the grip's profile (its finger channel and bulge), the prism's front rake, the mount boss and the eyepiece length.

mirrorless.depthNote: The model's 83 mm runs from the grip front to the back of the viewfinder eyecup, so it includes the eyecup; the DSLR's 78.5 mm leaves its eyepiece out, so the two depths are not directly comparable.
mirrorless.shapeNote: Traced from Nikon's manual drawings: the outline width, the viewfinder hump's width, the control positions. The model's own, generic shapes: the grip's profile (its finger channel and bulge), the hump's front rake and the mount boss.
